items.title: Report User — API & Validation
items.description: Implement POST /api/reports to allow users to report another user for inappropriate behavior, no-show, harassment, etc. Reports are linked to a specific session when applicable.
steps: POST /api/reports accepts CreateReportInput: { reportedId: string, sessionId?: string, reason: ReportReason, description?: string }
Validated with Zod schema from packages/shared-types
reporterId = authenticated user (req.user.id)
Cannot report yourself: if reportedId === req.user.id → return 400 'You cannot report yourself'
Reported user must exist: if no user found with reportedId → return 404 'User not found'
If sessionId provided: verify reporter was a participant in that session (user1Id or user2Id) → return 403 'You can only report users from sessions you participated in'
If sessionId NOT provided: verify reporter and reported have at least one shared session (any status) → return 403 'You can only report users you have had a session with'
Duplicate check: if report already exists with same reporterId + reportedId + sessionId → return 409 'You have already reported this user for this session'
Report created with status=OPEN
description field sanitized with sanitize-html before storage
Response: { report } with status 201
GET /api/reports — list reports filed BY the authenticated user (for their own reference)

Unit test: duplicate report → 409

items.title: Block User — API with Bidirectional Creation
items.description: Implement block/unblock endpoints. Blocking is bidirectional — always creates TWO Block records (A→B and B→A) so neither user can match with the other.
steps: POST /api/blocks accepts { blockedId: string }
Cannot block yourself: blockedId === req.user.id → return 400 'You cannot block yourself'
Blocked user must exist → return 404 if not found
If already blocked (Block record exists for blockerId=user + blockedId=target) → return 409 'User is already blocked'
Create TWO Block records in a single Prisma transaction: { blockerId: userId, blockedId: targetId } AND { blockerId: targetId, blockedId: userId }
This ensures bidirectional blocking — matching service already excludes blocked users from P2-02
Response: { success: true } with status 201
DELETE /api/blocks/:blockedId — unblock a user
Delete BOTH Block records (A→B and B→A) in a transaction
If no block exists → return 404 'Block not found'
Response: { success: true }
GET /api/blocks — list users the authenticated user has blocked
Returns array of { blockedId, blockedUser: { displayName, username, avatarUrl }, createdAt }
Verify matching service integration: create a block, then attempt booking in same slot — verify users are NOT matched
Unit test: bidirectional block creation (both records exist after POST)
Unit test: self-block rejected → 400
Unit test: duplicate block → 409
Unit test: unblock removes both records
Unit test: blocked users excluded from matching (integration test with MatchingService)

items.title: Input Sanitization — Full Audit
items.description: Verify ALL user-generated text is sanitized before storage to prevent XSS and injection attacks. This is a security-critical task.
steps: Install sanitize-html in apps/api
Install dompurify and @types/dompurify in apps/web
Create apps/api/src/utils/sanitize.ts with sanitizeInput(text: string): string function
sanitizeInput: uses sanitize-html with strict config — allowedTags: [] (no HTML tags at all), allowedAttributes: {}. Strips ALL HTML. Trims whitespace.
Create Zod transform helper: z.string().transform(sanitizeInput) — reusable across schemas
Audit and apply sanitization to ALL user-generated text fields before DB storage:
- User.displayName — sanitize in registration and profile update
- User.username — sanitize + validate alphanumeric/hyphens only (already should be via Zod regex)
- Session.user1Goal / user2Goal — sanitize in PATCH /api/sessions/:id/goal
- Reflection.text — sanitize in POST /api/reflections
- Report.description — sanitize in POST /api/reports
Update Zod schemas in packages/shared-types to include .transform(sanitizeInput) on all text fields, OR apply sanitization in the API service layer before Prisma create/update
Choose one approach and be consistent: EITHER sanitize in Zod transforms OR sanitize in service layer. Document the decision.
Frontend: create apps/web/lib/sanitize.ts with sanitizeForDisplay(text: string): string using DOMPurify
Frontend: all components that render user-generated text must use sanitizeForDisplay() or render as textContent (not innerHTML)
Verify: NO raw innerHTML or dangerouslySetInnerHTML anywhere in the codebase with user content
Search codebase for dangerouslySetInnerHTML — if found, either remove or wrap content in DOMPurify.sanitize()
Test: XSS payload '<script>alert(1)</script>' in displayName → stored as 'alert(1)' (tags stripped)
Test: XSS payload in goal text → stripped
Test: XSS payload in reflection text → stripped
Test: XSS payload in report description → stripped
Test: HTML entities preserved correctly: 'Tom & Jerry' stays as 'Tom & Jerry' (not double-encoded)
Unit test: sanitizeInput strips script tags
Unit test: sanitizeInput strips event handlers (onerror, onclick)
Unit test: sanitizeInput preserves normal text
Unit test: sanitizeInput handles empty string and null gracefully

items.notes: This is a security audit task. Every user input that gets stored and later displayed is an XSS vector. Miss one and you have a vulnerability.

Data export: 1 req/hour per user

General API routes: 100 req/min per user (catch-all)
Webhook endpoints (/api/webhooks/*): no rate limit (but signature verification protects them)
Rate limiter implementation: use express-rate-limit with Redis store (rate-limit-redis) for distributed rate limiting
Install rate-limit-redis package
Configure Redis store using shared Redis connection
Rate limit responses: 429 with { error: 'Too many requests. Please try again later.', retryAfter: seconds }
Include Retry-After header in 429 responses
Unit test: rate limit triggers after threshold
Unit test: rate limit resets after window
